title: Check RMS screen for system faults as the first step during an Aviva/OPC issue call
summary: During an Aviva/OPC issue call, check the Geek+ RMS screen first to determine whether any system faults are present. This provides the initial evidence point before deeper Aviva/OPC diagnosis.
when_to_use: Use this as the first step on any phone call where the issue involves Aviva/OPC, to quickly establish whether system faults are present on the RMS screen.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Perform the initial RMS system-fault check and report what is shown on the RMS screen.
access_or_tools_needed: Ability to view and read system faults displayed on the RMS screen

visual_references.description: Training segment frame containing the instruction: 'first thing first, go to that RMS screen, see if any system faults' (phone call first step).

steps.title: Open the RMS screen and check for system faults
steps.purpose: Establish the first evidence point on the support call by determining whether system faults are present.
steps.instruction: On the support call, go to the RMS screen and look for system faults.
steps.expected_result: You can state whether the RMS screen shows any system faults.
steps.healthy_condition: The RMS screen displays system faults (or confirms none are present) so you can report the current fault state.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot access the RMS screen to view system faults.

actions.label: Open RMS and view system faults
actions.exact_action: Go to that RMS screen, see if any system faults.

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access the RMS screen, escalate to the appropriate support role to obtain the RMS evidence.

steps.title: Report what the RMS system-fault state shows (faults present vs none)
steps.purpose: Capture the initial RMS evidence needed to choose the next diagnostic direction for the Aviva/OPC issue call.
steps.instruction: If system faults are present, note what faults are shown. If no system faults are shown, proceed using the call approach that compares what was reported from Aviva against backend state (capturing enough notes for later diagnosis).
steps.expected_result: Either (a) you have recorded the specific system faults shown on RMS, or (b) you have recorded that no system faults are shown and captured enough notes to support later comparison.
steps.healthy_condition: Your notes clearly distinguish between 'system faults present' and 'no system faults shown' based on what is visible on the RMS screen.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot accurately determine the RMS fault state or cannot capture the fault details needed for later diagnosis.

actions.label: Note RMS faults when present
actions.exact_action: Note what faults are shown (for later diagnosis).

actions.label: Record 'no faults' when none are present
actions.exact_action: If no system faults are shown, proceed with the source-described approach of comparing what was reported from Aviva against backend state (capture enough notes for later diagnosis).

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot access the RMS screen, escalate to the appropriate support role to obtain the RMS evidence.

success_criteria: On the call, you can clearly report whether the RMS screen shows any system faults.
If faults are present, the specific faults shown on RMS are noted for later diagnosis.
healthy_conditions: RMS system-fault state is observable and reportable (faults present or none present).
failure_conditions: RMS screen is not accessible, preventing verification of system faults.
escalation_guidance: If you cannot access the RMS screen, escalate to the appropriate support role to obtain the RMS evidence.
